subtype: Approach: worrying so much that he stops practising [Pitfall]
passage:
Aadhya: Pradeep, you haven't practised your part today.
Pradeep: I can't, Didi. Every time I start, I see everyone laughing.
Aadhya: Nobody is going to laugh.
Pradeep: What if they do? My stomach hurts just thinking about it.
Aadhya: The show is in three days. You've done it twice all week.
Pradeep: I know! That's why I feel worse. I haven't practised, so I'll mess up, so I'm scared, so I don't practise.
Aadhya: That's going round in circles, Pradeep.
Pradeep: I know. But I still can't open the script.
He sat on the bed, the script closed beside him.

qa.q: How many days were left until the show?
qa.a: Three days were left until the show.

qa.q: What is Pradeep afraid of, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Pradeep is afraid that everyone will laugh, and the stomach ache and avoiding the script show how strong the fear is. 😰

qa.q: What alternative approach could Pradeep try, and why?
qa.a: Pradeep could practise just one line aloud with Aadhya listening, then add another. A tiny step is easier to begin than the whole script and can break the cycle.

qa.q: How does Aadhya see Pradeep's worry?
qa.a: Aadhya points out that the cycle goes round in circles and reminds Pradeep of the three days left, so Aadhya seems worried and wants to help.

grounding: A boy imagines everyone laughing and feels sick, so he avoids rehearsing, and with less practice he becomes more nervous in a worry cycle.

subtype: Approach: worrying so much that he stops practising [Pitfall]
passage: When Miss chose me for the class skit, I was happy for about one hour. Then I started imagining the hall full, everyone watching, someone laughing when I said my line wrong. My stomach churned. So I didn't practise. Every time Amma said, "Pema, let's do your lines," I said I had homework. If I didn't look at the script, I didn't have to feel it. But the day got closer, and I knew my lines less, so I felt worse, so I practised even less. My sister Aparna called it the worry circle. Two days before the show, she sat on my bed and said, "Read one line to me, bhai. Just one." I did. My hands shook.

qa.q: What did Aparna call the pattern?
qa.a: Aparna called it the worry circle.

qa.q: How did Pema feel when imagining the full hall?
qa.a: Pema felt afraid of being laughed at, with a churning stomach, and avoided the script to escape that feeling.

qa.q: What would you change first to break the worry circle, and why?
qa.a: Start with one line a day to someone kind, like Aparna, because a tiny, safe step lowers the fear so practice can grow.

qa.q: How does Pema's avoiding look to Amma?
qa.a: Amma keeps offering help and hears only "homework", so she may feel puzzled and a little worried.

grounding: It shows a boy so afraid of being laughed at that he avoids rehearsing, which makes him more nervous in a growing cycle.

subtype: Approach: worrying so much that he stops practising [Pitfall]
passage:
Class teacher's note, Class 3B, drama week
Divyansh has a short speaking part in our class play. For two weeks he has found reasons to miss rehearsal: a headache, a lost script, a trip to the washroom. Today I found him in the corridor, pale, and he said, "Ma'am, what if they laugh at me?" He had not practised at home either. I think the less he rehearses, the more frightened he gets, and the more frightened he gets, the less he rehearses. I sat with him for five minutes and we read his three lines together, quietly. Tomorrow I will let him rehearse alone with me first, then with two friends, then with the class. I have also called his mother.
- Usha

qa.q: How many lines does Divyansh have?
What was Divyansh feeling when he asked, "What if they laugh at me?"
qa.a: He was frightened of being laughed at, and pale with worry.

qa.q: What does Usha's plan get right, and what else could help?
qa.a: It builds up the audience slowly, alone, then two friends, then the class; practising at home with his mother could add more calm repetitions.

qa.q: How does Divyansh's avoidance look to his classmates at rehearsal?
qa.a: His classmates probably notice he keeps missing and may be confused or even annoyed, without knowing he is scared.

grounding: It shows a boy whose fear of being laughed at makes him avoid rehearsing, which makes him more nervous in a cycle.
